counterfactual_missing_items: No family history of recurrent epistaxis or telangiectasias is provided
No classic HHT telangiectasias on lips, oral mucosa, or fingertips are described
Abdominal ultrasound: No definite vascular malformation
decisive_items: repeated right-sided epistaxis without obvious trauma
Revealed vascular malformation with capillary dilation
Hemoglobin: Dropped from 124 g/L to 64 g/L over three months
response.rationale: R1 is favored because recurrent epistaxis, progressive anemia, and nasal endoscopy showing vascular malformation with capillary dilation form a coherent HHT-like bleeding/telangiectasia picture. R5 relies on facial erythema and capillary malformations but lacks epistaxis/nasal vascular lesion and is weakened by normal cranial CT; R2/R3/R4 rely on nonspecific cutaneous or limb findings.

rejected.why: PHACE requires posterior fossa or arterial anomalies and a facial hemangioma; the abnormal turbinate enhancement is nasal, not intracranial, and no raw span supports the cardiac defect.
Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber requires limb overgrowth and venous malformation, which are absent; only capillary malformations are present.
Ehlers-Danlos has no raw support spans; short fingers and clinodactyly are nonspecific and no skin/joint/bleeding features are provided.
Redundant append-only completion of R3 with no new independent raw evidence.
Redundant append-only completion of R4 with no raw support spans.
